newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-4,200 remains key test for rangebound FTSE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-4,200 remains key test for rangebound FTSE.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index was seen stuck in its recent trading range for the time being with key support at around the 4,200 level, chart analysts said on Monday.

The blue chip index has tracked between 4,200 and 4,350 since March 20 and would need to break above that latter level to indicate a challenge to record highs set around the middle of March, analysts said.
Yet a break below 4,200 would suggest a further decline was on the cards, to the 4,100 level or even below. By 0853 GMT the FTSE was down 6.7 points at 4,303.8.
Susan Rigg at Chart Analysis noted that the FTSE's rally last week had lost momentum and the index could drop back to the 4,200 level where it found support at the start of this month.
Rigg said the 4,125 level -- roughly its peak before the sharp rally which started in mid January -- could provide a support level if the index drops below 4,200.
Chris Chaitow at Robert Fleming said seasonal factors could suggest markets across Europe were poised to backtrack from their gains of earlier this year.
"We are passing out of the period when markets do best, which is from December 1 to May 1, and entering the time when they do worst, from May 2 to November 30," Chaitow said.
Chaitow repeated that the 4,200 is a key support for the UK index. "4,200 is the key to the FTSE," Chaitow said. "As long as it stays above that level, the bulls are in control."
